_what: COMMITTED MIRROR of public.ops_cron_ordering_contract and the schedules of the jobs it governs.
_why: ops_cron_ordering_contract declares, as DATA, that one cron job CONSUMES what another PRODUCES.
Production is enforced by mon_detect_cron_ordering_contract(), twice an hour. That detector is
correct and fails closed, but it can only speak AFTER a migration is live: a migration that
reschedules a contracted job passed every PR check, and the contract was violated that way at
~14:00Z on 2026-09-11. This mirror is the per-PR input that closes the review-time half
APPLY-AND-MIRROR IS ONE CHANGE (AGENTS.md). If you reschedule a contracted job, or add/change a
contract row, update this file in the SAME diff. scripts/verify-cron-ordering-contract.ts then
checks the gap arithmetic BEFORE the migration is applied, and its live half asserts this file
has not drifted from production's contract rows.
DO NOT fix a red check by lowering min_gap_minutes or deleting a row. The detector's own
do_not says it: fix the SCHEDULE. Lowering the floor re-creates the silent staleness the
contract exists to catch, and for this routine it is Prohibition 1 (docs/ops/BARRIER_ENGINEER.md
PART 6) — never weaken a barrier to make it green.
_semantics: gap = downstream_minute - upstream_minute, PLAIN subtraction, not modulo 60 — copied from the live detector on purpose. A consumer must trail its producer WITHIN the hour; one that runs first reads an input up to a full cycle stale. See scripts/lib/cronOrdering.ts.
_mirrored_through_migration_why: The NEWEST migration version in supabase/migrations/ whose SQL mentions ops_cron_ordering_contract. scripts/verify-cron-ordering-contract.ts recomputes this from the tree and fails if it does not match, so a migration that changes the contract without updating this file goes RED on its own PR. That is AGENTS.md's apply-and-mirror rule enforced from the diff alone — no secret, no network, and no SQL parsing. If you add such a migration, re-read production, update the rows/schedules above, and set this to the new version.

contract.why: resolve_english_city_overlay SELECTs FROM public.search_listings_ar, which sync_search_listings_ar writes. Floor raised 5 -> 9 on 2026-09-11: the sync's max runtime was re-measured at 487.9s (8.1 min) over 167 runs in 7 days.

sync_search_listings_ar() selects from listing_native_location_v2, a VIEW referencing the MATVIEW active_listing_ids_v2; jobid 17 refreshes that matview. Floor 7 min: jobid 17 max runtime 360.4s (6.0 min) over 168 runs in 7 days. (ops_incident #143) [2026-10-13, 🔧] satisfied_by_lock = location_pipeline:v1_refresh: migration 20260927224625 kept :20/:22 and made jobid 17 hold a TRANSACTION-scoped advisory lock to COMMIT with jobid 28 blocking on it (measured 2026-10-13: pg_locks granted on pid 754260 from 13:20:00, job 28 blocked 13:22:00 → 13:22:31). The floor stays 7; the detector checks the real commands take the lock before their work (cron_contract_lock_satisfied) and only then skips the gap.

sync_search_listings_ar() reads loc_display_district_canon, the ONE canonical user-visible district rendering per (city_id, normalised district) required by SEARCH_MATCH_QA_ENGINEER.md §42.1; jobid 109 rebuilds it. Floor 2 min: jobid 109 max runtime 6.9s over 125 runs in 7 days.

refresh_loc_canonical_district() adds every district word the sync served (source live) to the Filter district list. Run before the sync finishes, it misses the words that sync carried in and the customer cannot pick a district the cards show until the next rebuild (2026-10-18: «العنبرية», المدينة المنورة, 41 ads). Floor 9 min = the sync's measured max runtime 8.1 min, as in contract 1.

The strip removes a platform's default point from the stored rows; the :22 sync then serves those ads without a pin so the district border shows (owner 2026-10-19). Run after the sync, the default point is served for an extra hour.

The strip removes a pin > 150 km from the ad's own city from the stored row; the :22 sync then serves that ad with the city/district border (owner 2026-10-20 «A»). Run after the sync, the far pin is served for an extra hour.

_gaps_as_measured: refresh_listing_native_location_v1 :20 -> sync-search-listings-ar :22 = 2 min (floor 7) — satisfied by the advisory lock location_pipeline:v1_refresh, not by the clock

lock_dependencies.why: Both commands take pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('location_pipeline:v1_refresh')) as their first real statement; pg_cron runs each command as ONE transaction, so the consumer blocks until the producer COMMITS the refreshed matviews (20260927224625; proven 2026-10-13, 🔧 proof row 1055).
